subtopic: Multi-Stage Builds and Docker Layer Caching
question_text: [Container Orchestration (Kubernetes) - Q18] Why does placing `COPY package.json .` and `RUN npm install` before `COPY . .` in a Dockerfile dramatically speed up iterative CI builds?

options.text: It forces Docker to compile packages in parallel
Docker caches layer results; if `package.json` has not changed, Docker reuses the cached `npm install` layer, avoiding downloading dependencies on source code edits
It reduces the size of the Linux kernel image

answer_explanation: Docker layer cache invalidation cascades downwards. Placing infrequently changing dependency files first ensures that daily source code edits do not invalidate the cached dependency install step.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Docker layer cache invalidation cascades downwards. Placing infrequently changing dependency files first ensures that daily source code edits do not invalidate the cached dependency install step.
